name: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
problem: KV cache quantization is applied per-token to both keys and values, which is exactly wrong for keys and wastes most of the value cache's headroom.
mechanism: A distribution study of KV elements on LLaMA / Falcon / Mistral establishes the asymmetry that drives everything: KEYS must be quantized PER-CHANNEL (group elements along the channel dimension) while VALUES must be quantized PER-TOKEN. Implementation matches: per-channel key quantization and per-token value quantization, each with its own group size, tuned-free. The channel/token split also happens to align with how the attention kernel reads memory, so it is hardware-coherent rather than merely statistically better.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): LLaMA / Falcon / Mistral 'maintain almost the same quality while using 2.6x LESS PEAK MEMORY (including model weight)'. COMPRESSION RATIO: 2-bit KV cache vs FP16 = 8x on the cache itself; the 2.6x figure is whole-model peak memory INCLUDING weights, which is the more honest number and the one to quote. QUALITY COST: 'almost the same quality' - not a paired delta in the abstract.
